MANILA, Philippines – Police arrested 276 individuals in Muntinlupa City on Sunday, November 16, most of whom were supposed to join a protest in Manila on the opening day of the 49th ASEAN Summit.
Some student journalists were also reportedly among those arrested.
In Liwasang Bonifacio, police arrested another 11 individuals as tensions rose between officers and protesters.
In an interview with GMA News, Southern Police District Director Rodel Pastor said the protesters had been camping out on the streets, outside a designated freedom park.
Those arrested were taken to Camp Bagong Diwa.
Several groups criticized the mass arrests carried out by the Philippine National Police (PNP), calling for accountability and the release of those detained.
Karapatan denounced what it described as police brutality and demanded accountability from the officers and commanders involved.

“These disturbing scenes, recorded in full public view, expose the brutality of the police and the extent to which state forces are willing to go to suppress dissent. The PNP has turned a public space meant for the exercise of people’s democratic rights into a site of violence and repression,” Karapatan secretary seneral Kristina Palabay said in a statement on Sunday.
Amnesty International Philippines also called the mass arrests into question and urged authorities to immediately release those detained.

“Protest marches that attempt to go beyond designated spaces or barricades, are still protected by the right to peaceful assembly, and must not be forcibly or violently dispersed,” the organization said.
Human rights lawyer and Karapatan deputy secretary general Maria Sol Taule said the PNP was wasting government resources by arresting around 300 individuals.
She cited the mass arrests during the September 21, 2025 protests. Most of the cases involved, she said, were eventually dismissed.
Muntinlupa Mayor Ruffy Biazon, meanwhile, criticized the violence that took place in his city.
“Ang pagpapahayag ng saloobin ay isang karapatang dapat igalang, at ang pagpapanatili ng kapayapaan at kaayusan ay dapat isinasagawa nang hindi isinasantabi ang karapatang pantao,” Biazon said.
(Freedom of expression is a right that must be respected, and the maintenance of peace and order must be carried out without disregarding human rights.)
Biazon said that the city government had deployed a medical team to assist those injured. – Rappler.com
